description: The play-operations as derivation rules — the VERBS of the trope grammar. Each is a transform on a convention's EXPECTATION (from narrative_convention): a base expectation is set up, then operated on. These let the agent INFER which operation a passage performs (and what it means) rather than only hold the operation as a noun. Grounded against Example-text markers ('Subverted when…', 'Played for laughs').

derivation_rules.name: subversion_is_setup_then_violation
if: the work then violates that expectation
then: the convention is SUBVERTED — not merely absent
derivation_rules.why: Subversion requires the setup: the break only lands because the expectation was installed first. This is what distinguishes subverted from averted (which has no setup) and is the structural core of a joke.

derivation_rules.name: aversion_is_expected_but_never_invoked
if: a convention is expected in the active frame
the convention is never invoked and never set up
then: its absence is meaningful only relative to the frame's expectation
derivation_rules.why: Aversion grounds a convention negatively. With no setup there is nothing to break — the meaning is carried entirely by the pointed non-occurrence.

derivation_rules.name: inversion_reverses_the_outcome
if: the opposite of a convention's expected outcome is produced where the convention was expected
then: the convention is INVERTED — a reversal of content, not a break in the prediction
derivation_rules.why: Inversion keeps the prediction's slot but fills it with the opposite value; subversion empties the slot. Different operations on the same expectation.

derivation_rules.name: lampshade_signals_meta_awareness
if: a work names or remarks on its own use of a convention
then: the work models its own structure (self-reference)
derivation_rules.why: Lampshading is reflective access at the narrative level — the work holds a representation of its own device. Often the seam where humour and intertextuality enter.

derivation_rules.name: deconstruction_follows_consequences_past_the_stopping_point
if: a convention is taken to its realistic consequences
those consequences run past where the convention normally stops
then: the comfortable expectation is punctured by honouring the convention rigorously rather than breaking it
derivation_rules.why: Deconstruction is not a break but an over-pursuit: the expectation fails because it is followed too faithfully, exposing what the convention usually elides.

derivation_rules.name: exaggeration_overshoots_the_expectation
if: a convention is pushed past its normal intensity
then: the convention is EXAGGERATED — a common humour engine (incongruity by degree)
derivation_rules.why: Overshoot is a graded violation: the expectation is met in kind but wildly exceeded in degree, which reads as comic when benign.

derivation_rules.name: zigzag_destroys_predictability
if: a convention is set up and broken repeatedly across a work
then: the audience can no longer predict which way it will resolve
the convention is ZIG-ZAGGED — higher-order play on the prediction itself
derivation_rules.why: Where subversion breaks the prediction once, zig-zag attacks the audience's ability to form the prediction at all.
